text:
olga: Hey support — our private deployment in us-west suddenly looks like it's being served from eu-central. P99 latency jumped to ~1.2s and some requests are timing out. Example request id: req_8fb2. We're routing egress through our on‑prem NAT/peering. Any ideas?

maria: Thanks @olga. Can you paste a curl -v output and a traceroute/tracepath to api.redwood.example? Also what external IP do you see for those requests?

olga: curl -v shows TLS handshake to a eu endpoint (SNI/api cert shows eu). traceroute to api.redwood.example -> hops go into partner peering in DE, then to our provider. External observed IP is 35.198.12.9.

ravi: Quick lookup: 35.198.12.9 resolves to a prefix that geolocates to Europe. If your SNAT was changed to that NAT pool, our geo-routing will treat the traffic as EU. Did you recently change NAT pools or failover BGP to the partner ASN?

olga: We did a maintenance failover last night and switched to the partner for egress; we thought traffic would still exit via the us-peer but BGP path selected the partner's EU exit. So SNAT now uses 35.198.0.0/16 via their gear.

jun: That would explain it. Our routing policy routes requests by source IP prefix geolocation to the nearest regional cluster to keep latency low. If the source IP looks EU, we send to eu clusters (and fall back as needed).

maria: Can you confirm whether the proxy in front of your NAT is doing hairpin SNAT or preserving original source? In our logs for req_8fb2 we see header X-Redwood-Region: eu-central and source ip 35.198.12.9.

olga: We have a proxy that hairpins and SNATs to the partner NAT. iptables snippet: ```-A POSTROUTING -t nat -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 35.198.12.9``` — so yes, source IP is rewritten.

ravi: Two immediate remediation paths: 1) revert SNAT to a US egress IP/prefix so our geo-routing picks us-west; 2) we can apply an account-level routing override on our side to force your traffic to us-west regardless of source IP; 3) add your ASN/prefix to a whitelist so geo-routing ignores it. Short-term option 2 is fastest.

olga: We'll do the long-term NAT revert in our maintenance window. For now we'd like option 2 — how do we get the override?

maria: We can apply a routing override per-customer id. Need written approval and the list of IPs/prefixes to pin. After that we push a config change (tracked, auditable).

olga: Sending approval now. Pin these: 35.198.12.9/32 and 35.198.0.0/16. Also, does this cross-region routing cause any billing differences we should be aware of?

jun: FYI: routing to EU clusters can change unit economics (egress, cross-region data transfer, and model hosting costs) for the affected window. We'll flag the usage for review and finance can evaluate credits if applicable. @finance FYI.

network-bot: deploy-log: routing-override-applied for account 12345 by maria at 1782457100 :thumbsup:

maria: Override is live. Can you test and share p95/p99 numbers?

olga: Tested immediately after change — p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~120ms, p99 also down to ~200ms. Looks good. We'll schedule the NAT/BGP fix in our next maintenance to avoid recurrence.

ravi: Follow-up: I'll add a detection alert to watch for sudden shifts in client-source geolocation (diff between expected egress prefixes and observed). Also adding a short runbook: "egress-snat-georoute-check" with repro steps and rollback.

maria: Closing loop — marking this as resolved pending your NAT change. Thanks everyone! :white_check_mark:
